title: China's Tech Stocks Are Falling Despite Their Own Breakthroughs - The Wire China
gist: Chinese tech equities sold off in the same fortnight that China delivered three decade-long industrial-policy goals — CXMT's DRAM IPO, a domestically produced DUV lithography tool, and Moonshot's frontier-class Kimi K3 — because each breakthrough adds subsidised capacity and destroys pricing power rather than creating profit. The piece argues involution (neijuan) plus open-weight AI means China can lead the world in capability while remaining a poor place to own the equity, with state 'national team' buying of roughly 60 billion yuan masking the gap onshore but not in Hong Kong.

themes.theme: The sell-off into three sovereignty milestones

insights.claim: Shanghai's STAR 50 index has surrendered much of a rally that had lifted it roughly 70 percent between April and July, while the CSI 300 sits about 9 percent below its late-June peak and the Hang Seng Tech Index has underperformed for months.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Sizes the drawdown: a 70 percent Q2 melt-up in Chinese tech has largely round-tripped, so positioning is being unwound rather than merely trimmed.
insights.locator: China’s technology shares have spent the past fortnight

insights.claim: Chinese equity investors sold every sector that produced China's three biggest technology milestones in a decade — a DRAM national champion listing, a domestic DUV lithography tool, and a frontier-class open-weight model — all delivered within the same two weeks.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Technological success is no longer a buy signal in Chinese tech; treat capability headlines as potential sell catalysts in a subsidised, overcapacity market.
insights.quote: Three triumphs for technological sovereignty: and yet investors in China’s stock markets sold every category that produced them.

insights.claim: A state-owned Chinese manufacturer was reported to have moved a home-grown deep-ultraviolet lithography tool into production, cracking a step in advanced chipmaking that the West, through ASML, assumed it still controlled.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: If confirmed, this removes the West's most durable chokepoint on Chinese chipmaking and is the single most consequential item in the sequence for ASML's terminal value.
insights.locator: A state-owned domestic manufacturer was reported

insights.claim: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 is the closest China has come to American frontier models since the AI race began in 2022.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The capability gap argument for premium U.S. model pricing is weakening at exactly the moment investors are demanding AI monetization proof.
insights.locator: Finally, Moonshot AI released Kimi K3

insights.claim: The sell-off is explained by the widening gap between the technical capability of Chinese technology companies and their profitability, a gap onshore markets have not yet fully priced.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The core framework for Chinese tech: underwrite margins, not milestones — and assume onshore prices still have further to fall toward the offshore verdict.
insights.quote: it can easily be explained by the gap between the growing technical capability of Chinese tech companies, and their profitability
insights.locator: While such a sell-off might look surprising

insights.claim: CXMT's July 27 STAR market IPO was read as a warning rather than a triumph, because it signals another heavily subsidised entrant racing to add memory capacity into a market already braced for a price war.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Bearish for global DRAM pricing and for incumbent memory margins — a listed, capital-raising CXMT can fund capacity expansion through a downcycle.
insights.quote: the warning being that another heavily subsidised entrant would now be racing to add capacity into a market already braced for a price war
insights.locator: In memory chips, CXMT’s arrival on the stock market

insights.claim: A genuine Chinese DUV machine would erode the pricing power of ASML's quasi-monopoly and potentially commoditize a category of currently very expensive semiconductor equipment.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The threat to ASML is margin compression through competition, not export-control-driven volume loss — a different and more permanent impairment.
insights.quote: it will erode the pricing power of what to date, in the form of ASML, has been a quasi-monoply, potentially commoditizing these currently very expensive pieces of equipment
insights.locator: The milestone reached in advanced lithography carries the same double edge

insights.claim: Open weights structurally strip the model layer of pricing power — anyone can run the model so no one can charge a premium — turning the token into a commodity export with a frontier-class Chinese model running at a fraction of the Western list price.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Value in AI accrues below or above the model layer, not at it — a direct argument against paying for model-layer equity anywhere in the world.
insights.quote: But open weights, by design, strip the model layer of pricing power. Anyone can use the model, so no one can charge a premium for it.
insights.locator: Nowhere is the divergence starker than in artificial intelligence

insights.claim: China's open-weight strategy makes companies from DeepSeek to Moonshot the global price-setters in AI models and a genuine force in worldwide adoption, even as it leaves them with almost no visible profit at the point of production.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Chinese labs set the global price floor for intelligence without capturing the rent — the deflationary force in AI comes from firms indifferent to their own margins.
insights.quote: The result is the peculiar spectacle of world-class technical achievement generating almost no visible profit at the point where it is produced.
insights.locator: A frontier-class Chinese model now runs at a fraction

insights.claim: A sector can lead the world in technical capability and still be a poor place in which to seek market gains, which is why the roster of listed Chinese model companies producing breakthroughs are not good investments.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Separates the national-capability thesis from the equity thesis — a reusable rule for any state-subsidised strategic sector.
insights.quote: A sector can lead the world in capability and still be a poor place in which to seek market gains.
insights.locator: That is precisely the problem for equity investors

themes.theme: State support masking the onshore signal

insights.claim: Beijing's 'national team' funds — China Reform Holdings, China Chengtong and peers — recently deployed roughly 60 billion yuan (nearly $9 billion) to prop up falling AI-related stocks, partly stemming the market bleeding.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Onshore Chinese tech prices contain an ~$9bn state bid — a support level that can be withdrawn, and evidence the unsupported clearing price is lower.
insights.quote: have recently deployed roughly 60 billion yuan (nearly $9 billion) to prop up falling AI-related stocks
insights.locator: Beijing’s “national team” of large investment funds

insights.claim: The stock-buyback re-lending facility the People's Bank of China set up in September 2024 has materially reduced the cost of state market intervention.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: China has built a cheap, standing mechanism for equity price support — expect drawdowns to be dampened onshore regardless of fundamentals.
insights.locator: A stock-buyback re-lending facility which China’s central bank set up

insights.claim: Hong Kong provides the unfiltered investor verdict: on the day the DUV news broke, mainland money rotated out of Hong Kong technology stocks into financials and consumer names, leaving the headline index flat while the tech sub-index sagged.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Use Hong Kong tech versus onshore STAR as the cleanest read on true sentiment toward China's tech-sovereignty story, and note the rotation destination was financials and consumer.
insights.quote: Investors were not buying the tech sovereignty story. They were selling the companies that are at the forefront of achieving this state-led goal.
insights.locator: In Hong Kong, the verdict of investors is relatively unfiltered

themes.theme: External amplifiers: contagion and the AI mood shift

insights.claim: The DUV lithography report sent Korea's Kospi down more than 10 percent in a single session and dragged the Nikkei and ASML lower, with Chinese chip names unable to decouple from a regional rout their own country's advance had triggered.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A single Chinese equipment headline is now capable of a 10 percent one-day move in a G20 index — Asian semiconductor complexes are correlated to Chinese capability news in both directions.
insights.quote: The same DUV report that thrilled China’s industrial strategists sent Korea’s Kospi down more than 10 percent in a single session and dragged the Nikkei and ASML down with it.

insights.claim: Global markets have turned skeptical of the AI trade and are demanding evidence of monetization to justify the capital already sunk into it, a shift made worse by a more hawkish Federal Reserve.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The regime has flipped from rewarding AI capex to demanding AI cash flow — capability announcements now land as bear ammunition rather than upside catalysts.
insights.quote: China’s breakthroughs did not arrive into an enthusiastic market; they arrived as fresh ammunition for the bears.

insights.claim: Chinese AI breakthroughs are real and advance China's strategic autonomy, but will not translate into corporate profits as long as leading Chinese models remain open weight and the involution problem persists.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The two named conditions — a shift away from open weights, or genuine capacity discipline — are the specific triggers to watch before re-rating Chinese tech equity.
insights.quote: It is hard to see how this might change if the country’s leading AI models remain open weight and the involution problem remains intact.
insights.locator: All in all, while Chinese companies’ breakthroughs in AI are real
